tasks.title: Audit robots.txt, sitemap.xml and canonical tags on all zedu.chat marketing pages

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Fix the Lighthouse SEO audits we can already predict, then re-run Lighthouse to confirm
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The goal's test is a Lighthouse SEO score of 90, so start from what Lighthouse checks, not from guesses. Checked on 22 Oct 2026 with curl and a 375 px headless Chrome run: 1) zedu.chat/robots.txt returns the site's HTML page (text/html), not a robots file, so Lighthouse's 'robots.txt is valid' check should fail. 2) /auth/sign-up and /auth/login have the bare title 'Zedu' and no meta description tag, so 'document has a meta description' should fail on both. 3) At 375 px, many links and buttons are smaller than the recommended tap size (19 of 37 on /pricing, and 7 of 10 on /auth/sign-up in one run), which Lighthouse's tap-target check flags. Two things named in the goal looked fine in my sample: no broken links from the home page (37 internal and 7 outside links all returned 2xx or 3xx) and every one of the 26 home page images has alt text, though one alt reads like a file name ('socials-row').

Approach: 1) Run Lighthouse's SEO category on 10 key pages (home, pricing, three product pages, three solutions pages, sign-up, login) and record each failing audit with its score. 2) Fix only what fails: a real robots.txt and sitemap, titles and descriptions for sign-up and login, tap target sizes, the one file-name alt text. 3) Re-run the same 10 pages and report before and after, with the score per page. Tasks: Lighthouse baseline (seo), the fix list with paste-ready code (seo), re-run and compare (research).

Limit: I have not run Lighthouse yet, so the predicted failures above are inferences from the audits' published rules; the baseline run confirms or corrects them.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Make unknown URLs return a real 404 instead of a 200 app shell, and lock it with a crawl check
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Checked 22 Oct 2026: zedu.chat/security and other URLs that do not exist return HTTP 200 with a few words of app shell and canonical https://zedu.chat. The client catch-all turns every typo, dead backlink and guessed URL into an indexable empty page, so Google can waste crawl on routes with no content and real 404s are never reported. Work: list the public routes and their current status codes; find the catch-all that swallows unknown paths; make genuinely unknown org and page slugs return a real 404 with a useful page while valid workspace routes still load; verify 10 known and 10 unknown URLs by curl with before and after status and body size; add the check to the monthly SEO script so it cannot regress. Deliver the status table, the code diff and the first regression run. Distinct from the Lighthouse workstreams: Lighthouse SEO does not test soft 404s or what Google is allowed to index.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Score-gated fix loop: fix titles, broken links and alt text in priority order until each core page clears Lighthouse 90
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The goal already names its success test: Lighthouse 90 or better, through three defect classes. I propose one measured pass instead of a scattergun audit. 1) Baseline: run Lighthouse (mobile) on the ten core marketing routes and record per-page scores plus the failing audits for meta titles/descriptions, broken links, and alt text. 2) Fix in priority order: first missing or duplicate titles and meta descriptions, then every link that returns 404 (replace with the live equivalent or remove), then descriptive alt text on all images. 3) Re-run Lighthouse after each fix batch and keep going until every core page clears 90. Done when: a per-page before/after score table exists (with the Lighthouse report attached for each run), the exact file changes for every fix are listed, and any page that still cannot reach 90 has a written reason (for example a third-party script) so the owner can accept the remainder knowingly. Measured: pages at 90+ before vs after, count of 404s fixed, count of images given real alt text. Why this fits: the goal names the defect classes and the threshold; this idea turns them into a fixed order of work with evidence at each step, and claims nothing beyond what Lighthouse itself reports. Scoped to Lighthouse-90 evidence; it will not duplicate the other SEO goals' metadata or claim-audit workstreams.
